Hi Samir — thanks for flagging this. Totally understand the confusion around the Mar 8 US DST switch (EU doesn't move until the end of March). We try to avoid "floating" local times in cross-region invites for exactly this reason.

Two quick agreements from our side:
1) We'll reissue the invite with the timezone locked to UTC (recommended) and include the explicit local equivalents for ET, CET, and IST in the body.
2) I’m attaching three concrete alternative slots (UTC-first) so your attendees can pick the one that keeps people in reasonable local hours. Proposed slots (all in UTC):
   - A) 2026-03-09 14:00 UTC (9:00 AM ET / 14:00 CET)
   - B) 2026-03-09 16:00 UTC (11:00 AM ET / 16:00 CET)
   - C) 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC (4:00 AM ET — low for US, so less preferred but OK for APAC)

We recommend A or B; A keeps it mid-morning ET and late afternoon CET. I attached a .ics (proposed_slots.ics) and a short note with SOC2 summary (SOC2-summary-redwood.pdf). Ben will confirm which engineers can join for the later slot if you prefer B. Jonas can cover APAC-friendly hours next week if needed.

If you confirm A or B I'll send the locked UTC invite and copy procurement/security on the updated calendar entry.

Thanks — Marissa
